jonah (pm): quick sync  Competitor Y launched a per-index credit model that undercuts our hosted price for bulk indexing. customers are asking if we can offer a cheaper *storage/index* path vs per-request. thoughts? :thinking:
maria: interesting. different vector: they're selling price for one-time bulk indexing rather than low-latency queries. could be an upsell hole for us (cold index vs hot query).
rachel (ml): technical trade: we can compress embeddings (FP16 -> 8-bit or product quant) for storage and do on-the-fly upconversion for queries. quality loss depends on downstream task (search vs semantic similarity). we need a matrix.
igor (eng): infra cost: compressed storage helps S3/egress costs, but on-the-fly decode adds CPU on query path unless we pre-warm. two implementation paths: (A) store compressed + decode at read; (B) do nightly decompress for hot shards. both need routing rules. ballpark: 3 sprints to prototype path A.
kevin (ops): ops impact: more IO and CPU variability. we should track decode latency and also storage-savings per TB. will need a new meter: "embedding-storage-credits" to tie to billing.
laura (sales): sellers prefer simple promises: "cheap for archival index" and a straightforward price. If we can promise X% cheaper for cold indexing with a clear caveat on latency for real-time queries, sales can push it.
amelia (research): propose experiment grid: vary compression (8-bit, 4-bit PQ), and routing (pre-decompress hot shards vs decode-on-read). test on 5 customer corpora across search and similarity tasks. measure precision@10, recall@100, and end-to-end query p95.
rachel (ml): agree. add adversarial queries (rare names, long docs) to catch non-linear degradation. require guardrail: precision@10 drop <= 3% for archival use-case.
jonah (pm): product options we can evaluate in parallel: 1) Index-Credit Packs: one-time bulk upload credit with compressed storage; 2) "Cold Index" tier: cheaper per-embed storage + longer tail query latency; 3) Keep-as-is but add a storage rebate for customers who pre-batch uploads. which to prioritize for an MLP?
maria: prioritize 1 + 2 together: customers want bundled purchasable credits (1) and a named tier (2). keep per-request pricing stable. we need launch gates though.
igor (eng): canary plan for path A (decode-on-read):
```
canary: tenant-cohort A (3 customers) -> compressed storage, decode-on-read
metrics: p95 query latency, precision@10 delta, decode-cpu usage
failure conditions: precision@10 drop > 3% OR p95 latency increase > 200ms
rollout: 1% traffic -> 10% -> 50% over 7 days with auto-fallback
```
kevin (ops): provision note: will need a temporary burst pool for decode CPU; estimate +3 vCPUs per node for canary. deploy-bot: request created for 2 c5d instances.
laura (sales): pricing experiment idea: sell 10k-index-credit pack at 70% of hosted price for archival usage, show side-by-side TCO for customers. i'll test with two pilot accounts.
amelia (research): owners & deliverables: - rachel + amelia: bench matrix + adversarial shard by Fri EOD - igor + kevin: infra spike + canary playbook by Tue - laura: pricing pilot offers by Wed - jonah: product docs + launch gates draft by Thu.
maria: launch gates (draft): - archival precision@10 gap <= 3% - decode-on-read p95 < 400ms for archival queries - storage savings >= 40% per TB - clear opt-in & labeled "Cold Index" in Console; not available on Dedicated at GA
jonah (pm): small poll: react with :thumbsup: if you prefer Index-Credit Packs first, :eyes: for Cold-tier first.
igor (eng): noted. starting infra spike now.
deploy-bot: provisioning request submitted (2 x c5d) pending approval.
maria: thanks everyone. try to keep experimental telemetry surfaced to Sales so they can present realistic tradeoffs.
